items.title: Voter turnout way up during advance polling in Mississauga
items.summary: More than 44,000 people in Mississauga cast their ballots early at advance voting stations over the past week in the leadup to the 2026 municipal election, the city says. The 44,049 advance votes cast during the six days of early voting between Oct. 6-11 set a new mark for the city and represents a 57 per cent increase compared to advance voting in the 2022 municipal election, the City of Mississauga said on Tuesday. Voters in Canada’s seventh-largest city cast 28,052 early ballots four years ago and 19,188 in the weeks prior to the 2018 municipal election, according to numbers provided by the City of Mississauga. During the 2024 mayoral byelection in Mississauga, 24,731 people went to the polls early. The number of 2026 early ballots cast by day, the city noted, were as follows: “The strong participation during advance voting is encouraging,” Diana Rusnov, City of Mississauga clerk and director of legislative services, said. ” With advance voting over, the next and final chance for eligible residents to cast their ballots is election day, Oct. 26. m. m. On election day, residents can vote at any voting location within their ward. They’ll be casting ballots for mayor of Mississauga (14 candidates), city councillors (11 wards) and school board trustees.

items.title: ‘Dark web’ drug bust leads police to 600 grams of fentanyl and charges for Mississauga man
items.summary: An investigation into drugs bought on a “dark web marketplace” being shipped through the mail has led to charges for a man from Mississauga, police say. The Caledon Community Street Crime Unit and officers with the Covert Internet Intelligence Unit began investigating suspected drug shipments earlier in the summer, the OPP says in a release on Tuesday. Police believed a high volume of drugs was being bought on the dark web and moved through the mail. Officers say they arrested a suspect on Aug. 25 at a Canada Post location in Mississauga, and seized two packages containing various drugs that were to be shipped to addresses across Canada. The arrest led to police raids of several residences and vehicles within the Greater Toronto Area, and the OPP says officers seized approximately 600 grams of suspected fentanyl, approximately 35 grams of suspected cocaine, $40,000 in Canadian currency, drug trafficking paraphernalia and numerous electronic devices. The OPP says Jermoll Bain, 33, of Mississauga, has been charged with 16 counts of failure to comply with release order, nine counts of possession of proceeds obtained by crime over $5,000, and trafficking-related offences. Jermaine Willis, 34, of North York, has also been charged with possession of proceeds obtained by crime over $5,000. Bain was scheduled to make a court appearance in Brampton on Tuesday, while Willis will make a court appearance on Oct. 29.

items.title: Bike lanes gone as city launches new plan for major street in Mississauga
items.summary: The city has removed bike lanes from a busy street in Mississauga’s north end as it moves forward with a plan to reintroduce a fourth lane of traffic. A City of Mississauga spokesperson confirmed to INSAUGA Canada on Tuesday the bicycle lanes that were introduced in 2023 as part of a pilot project have been eliminated from a large stretch of Aquitaine Avenue in Meadowvale. In addition to the extra lane for vehicles, the new plan also calls for an “in-boulevard, multi-use path” for cyclists and pedestrians along a section of the main avenue. The City of Mississauga road redesign follows a lengthy — and somewhat controversial — pilot study introduced three years ago that eliminated one lane of vehicle traffic on a section of Aquitaine Avenue and added bicycle lanes. The trial run was conducted to look at ways to improve safety for drivers, pedestrians and cyclists, the city said at the outset of the project, which received mixed reviews from the public. Many residents didn’t like the idea of removing one lane of traffic from the busy stretch of road. The Aquitaine Avenue Road Safety Pilot Project reduced a section of the busy four-lane road to three lanes in summer 2023 in an effort to make it safer and reduce speeding. It was among a number of road safety improvement initiatives introduced across the city. Image shows new design for Aquitaine Avenue moving forward. (Image: City of Mississauga) Following feedback from the community and guidance from new provincial legislation regarding bike lanes that took effect last December, the city decided to undo the Aquitaine Avenue pilot and reinstate a fourth lane for cars.

items.title: Record 44,000-Plus Ballots Cast in Mississauga's Advance Voting, Up 57 Per Cent From 2022
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, 44,049 residents cast ballots during advance voting for the 2026 municipal election. The city reports the advance polls ran from Oct. 6 to 11 at voting locations across Mississauga. City officials say that turnout marks a 57 per cent increase over the 2022 municipal election, when 28,052 ballots were cast in advance. The comparison, the city notes, sets a new high for advance-voting participation in Mississauga. Residents who have not yet voted can do so on Election Day, Oct. 26, at any voting location within their own ward, according to the city.

items.title: City Seeks Volunteers to Keep Mississauga's Neighbourhood Ice Rinks Running This Winter
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents can volunteer to help create and maintain natural ice rinks in neighbourhood parks this winter. The city says these rinks give residents free places to skate, play hockey and spend time outdoors through the cold months. Unlike larger skating facilities, the city notes natural ice rinks depend entirely on local volunteers to maintain the ice throughout the season. City officials say 102 volunteers helped run neighbourhood rinks during the 2025-2026 winter season. Residents interested in volunteering can apply online by Nov. 15, according to the city.

items.title: Hospitality Professional Sabir Masih Challenges Incumbent for Mississauga Ward 5 Catholic Trustee Seat
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports three candidates, including one incumbent and two challengers, are running for the Ward 5 trustee seat on the Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board. According to the outlet, Metroland sent a questionnaire to every name on the ballot to help voters compare the field. Candidate Sabir Masih told Metroland he works in hospitality and brings experience in education, leadership and community service. Masih said he has not previously held elected office, but has been actively engaged in community development and volunteer work. He said those experiences strengthened his commitment to public service, collaboration, accountability and listening to community needs.

items.title: Twenty-Year Ward 10 Resident Brea Corbet Defends DPCDSB Seat Against Two Challengers
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports three candidates are competing for the Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board trustee seat covering Mississauga Wards 9 and 10, with incumbent Brea Corbet facing challengers Reshma Mathew and Mathew Thomas. According to the outlet, Metroland sent a questionnaire to everyone on the ballot so voters could compare their answers. Corbet told Metroland she has served as the elected DPCDSB trustee for Wards 9 and 10 since 2018. She said she has lived in Ward 10 for more than 20 years, raising her family there with her husband, and that all three of her children attended DPCDSB schools in the ward. Corbet said that history gives her a close understanding of the neighbourhoods and the priorities of local families.

items.title: Toronto Real Estate Board Data Puts Average Mississauga Home Price at $929,600 for September
items.summary: According to the Toronto Regional Real Estate Board, the average home price in Mississauga reached $929,600 in September 2026, up 3.5 per cent from a year earlier. The board reports 468 homes sold in the city during the month, with properties spending an average of 36 days on the market and 2,408 active listings remaining at month's end. Among detached houses, TRREB recorded 196 sales with an average of 30 days on the market and 919 active listings. Semi-detached houses saw 72 sales over the same 30-day average, with 202 active listings. Attached houses posted 13 sales averaging 33 days on the market and 68 active listings, while townhouse-style condos recorded 61 sales averaging 41 days on the market and 373 active listings.
